title: Mixed at birth: ten long worlds

thesis.claim: Brains mixed at birth keep a world healthy and make it rich over a long life. In B2 with every newborn's brain mixed from its parent's and a neighbour's, at iteration 10,000, fewer than half the agents hold three tokens or fewer in the median world of ten, where three in four do in B2; and at least seven of the ten worlds meet every mark of the health bar.
thesis.why: In the pilots, the worlds whose brains were mixed at birth came closest of all to a world that is healthy and whose agents differ (Meta X). The two worlds of batch Q and their continuations meet every mark of the health bar, at a dimension of 3.4 to 3.9, with 15% to 52% of their agents at three tokens or fewer: 37% and 20% at 2,000 iterations, 38% and 19% at 5,500 and 7,500. Mixed with gifts as well, 39%, and with estates shared by wealth, 31%, at 1,000 iterations, with six marks each. B2's own worlds hold 70% to 78% of their agents at three tokens or fewer at 2,000 iterations (Experiment 16) and 66% to 79% at 9,500 to 10,000 (the same worlds played on as pilots), and nine in ten of them meet six marks: their dimension is 4.2 to 4.8, above the bar's 4. A mixed world is a quarter to a third of B2's size, so its agents hold more each, and a unit of a brain that works can spread from one line to another. But one of the two continuations swung back towards B2's poverty at 2,500 iterations, half its agents at three tokens or fewer, before it recovered: it may not last.
thesis.confirm: At iteration 10,000, each world read from its last checkpoint as research/atlas/profile.py reads every world (Meta X): the median of the ten worlds' shares of agents holding three tokens or fewer is below 0.5, and at least seven of the ten worlds meet all seven marks of Chapter 46's health bar — one piece, a 2-core of at least 0.8, no agent whose loss cuts off more than 2% of the others, no link more than 1%, no agent joined to more than 5% of the others, 3 to 12 links per agent, a dimension of 2.3 to 4.
thesis.refute: A median share of 0.5 or more, or fewer than seven worlds meeting every mark: mixing at birth does not keep a world rich and healthy over a long life.
